packageText: TITLE: Functional Ovarian Cyst SOURCE STATUS - [Both] This fused master source combines RadPrimer Functional Ovarian Cyst with STATdx Functional Ovarian Cyst. - [RadPrimer] Canonical hierarchy: All Categories > Basic > Ultrasound > Female Pelvis Basic > Functional Ovarian Cyst - [RadPrimer] Canonical deck path: Corebook::Ultrasound::Female Pelvis Basic::Functional Ovarian Cyst - [Both] Core Radiology evidence was requested but not supplied in this browser bundle; do not label later output as Core-supported unless a later run provides auditable Core text. MASTER SUMMARY - [Both] Functional ovarian cysts are physiologic ovarian cysts of reproductive-age patients, mainly follicles/follicular cysts and corpus luteum/corpus luteum cysts. They are common, usually benign, and most resolve spontaneously. - [Both] A follicle is a thin-walled anechoic intraovarian cyst under 3 cm in a premenopausal patient. Larger simple anechoic cysts in premenopausal patients are also usually physiologic, but management depends on size and confidence of visualization. - [Both] A corpus luteum cyst is a thick-walled postovulatory cyst, usually with a hyperechoic wall, possible crenulated margin, central anechoic or hypoechoic cavity, hemorrhage/retracted clot, and marked peripheral Doppler flow. - [Both] Hemorrhagic functional cysts show lace-like/reticular internal echoes, retracting clot, fluid-fluid or fluid-debris level, and no true internal vascularity; Doppler flow belongs to the wall or surrounding ovarian tissue, not to clot. ULTRASOUND RECOGNITION - [Both] Transvaginal ultrasound is the best diagnostic tool. Confirm that the cyst is intraovarian by identifying surrounding ovarian parenchyma, follicles, or bridging ovarian tissue. - [RadPrimer] Exophytic ovarian cysts can mimic paraovarian or tubal lesions; bridging ovarian parenchyma is a helpful sign that the cyst arises from the ovary. - [Both] Follicular cysts are thin-walled and anechoic, with no increased internal Doppler flow. - [Both] Corpus luteum cysts occur after ovulation in the latter part of the menstrual cycle. They are thick-walled, may collapse into a crenulated shape, and may contain internal hemorrhage or retracting clot. - [Both] The ring-of-fire sign is marked peripheral vascular flow around a corpus luteum cyst wall. It is expected around the normal corpus luteum and is not specific for ectopic pregnancy. - [STATdx] A very vascular cyst margin can look alarming; do not mistake expected corpus luteum wall vascularity for an enhancing solid component unless vascular solid tissue is truly present. - [STATdx] Ruptured hemorrhagic cyst can show a hemorrhagic cyst plus moderate pelvic free fluid; free fluid may extend into the upper abdomen. - [STATdx] Large functional cysts may compress ovarian parenchyma to a thin rim. In a painful enlarged ovary, use pulse Doppler to document arterial and venous waveforms while remembering that Doppler flow does not fully exclude torsion. CT AND MR - [Both] CT is often obtained first in nonpregnant patients with acute pain, but it is limited for internal architecture of fluid-attenuation adnexal lesions. - [Both] On CT, a functional cyst is usually a low-attenuation adnexal mass unless hemorrhagic; hemorrhage may appear as high-attenuation blood products or a fluid-fluid level. Contrast CT may show an enhancing corpus luteum wall corresponding to ring-of-fire vascularity. - [Both] On MR, follicles are typically T2 hyperintense, T1 hypointense, and nonenhancing. Hemorrhagic cyst signal varies with blood-product age. DIFFERENTIAL AND PITFALLS - [Both] Ectopic pregnancy is the key mimic when a ring-of-fire adnexal lesion is present. A corpus luteum cyst is intraovarian and moves with the ovary; a tubal ectopic is usually separate from the ovary and may be displaced away from it with gentle probe pressure. - [Both] Ectopic pregnancy may have an extraovarian echogenic ring, adnexal hematoma, and echogenic free fluid. Heterotopic pregnancy is a consideration when there is an intrauterine pregnancy plus a separate tubal ectopic, especially after fertility treatment. - [Both] Ovarian neoplasms in the differential include benign cystic neoplasms such as serous cystadenoma, mucinous cystadenoma, and cystic teratoma; solid tumors such as thecoma-fibroma; and ovarian malignancy. - [Both] Persistent cystic mass after pregnancy, postmenopausal hemorrhagic-appearing cyst, growth without resolution, or solid vascular components should prompt concern for neoplasm rather than routine functional cyst follow-up. PATHOLOGY AND NATURAL HISTORY - [Both] A follicular cyst forms from a persistent follicle when ovulation does not occur and may be associated with elevated estrogen. - [Both] The corpus luteum forms from the graafian follicle after ovulation. It contains luteinized granulosa cells and a central cystic cavity with fluid/fibrin, often with hemorrhage. - [Both] If no embryo implants, the corpus luteum degenerates after about 14 days into the corpus albicans. With conception, human chorionic gonadotropin stimulates progesterone production until the placenta assumes progesterone production near the end of the second month. - [Both] Functional cysts occur during reproductive years. Most are asymptomatic, found incidentally, or found during fertility monitoring. Symptoms may result from capsular distention, rupture/ovulation pain, hemorrhage/hemoperitoneum, or torsion. - [Both] Corpus luteum cysts may enlarge early in pregnancy, peak around 7 weeks, and usually diminish with pregnancy progression; most are no longer seen by early second trimester. MANAGEMENT ORIENTATION - [Both] Malignancy rate in unilocular simple cysts is under 1%, and most functional cysts resolve spontaneously. - [RadPrimer] SRU 2019 simple cyst guidance for reproductive-age patients: up to 5 cm needs no follow-up; over 5 cm and up to 7 cm can have annual follow-up if confidently characterized, stopping if stable at 2 years; suboptimally evaluated cysts or cysts over 7 cm get short-interval characterization/resolution imaging and later growth-rate evaluation. - [Both] SRU hemorrhagic cyst guidance for reproductive-age patients: up to 5 cm needs no follow-up; over 5 cm gets follow-up ultrasound in about 6-12 weeks to ensure resolution. - [STATdx] O-RADS 2022 premenopausal functional cyst guidance: follicles/corpus luteum under 3 cm are O-RADS 1 with no follow-up; simple cysts 3-5 cm are O-RADS 2 with no follow-up; simple cysts over 5 cm and under 10 cm may get 12-month ultrasound follow-up with stopping at 24 months if stable. - [Both] Classic benign hemorrhagic cysts under 10 cm are O-RADS 2; under 5 cm needs no follow-up, while over 5-10 cm usually gets 8-12 week follow-up and referral/MR if persistent or enlarging. - [Both] Simple or hemorrhagic cysts over 10 cm are O-RADS 3 and should be managed with follow-up ultrasound and/or MR by gynecology. - [Both] If a mass decreases in size or resolves, it is benign. Growth without solid components suggests benign neoplasm growth. Solid components, especially with growth, increase malignancy concern. - [Both] Symptomatic treatment is appropriate for pain. Oral contraceptives may help recurrent cysts. Persistent symptomatic lesions may require laparoscopic fenestration or cystectomy with preservation of normal ovarian tissue. IMAGE CURATION SUMMARY - [Both] Actual image_evidence files were inspected with contact sheets before duplicate classification. - [Both] STATdx fully covers the RadPrimer image set as exact duplicates for images 1-4, proven by matching stable source image IDs and visual contact-sheet review. - [RadPrimer] RadPrimer images 1-4 remain the canonical primary copies because RadPrimer is the hierarchy/backbone source. - [STATdx] STATdx images 1-4 are archived as optional exact duplicates of RadPrimer images 1-4. STATdx images 5-14 remain selected primary images because they add distinct visual examples and pitfall/complication reinforcement. - [Both] No source case cluster was intentionally split. PRIMARY IMAGE APPENDIX - RadPrimer image 1: Graphic shows a functional ovarian cyst arising exophytically from the ovary . Note bridging ovarian parenchyma between the ovary and ovarian cyst, which is a helpful clue that this is indeed a cyst arising from the ovary rather than from an adjacent structure. Teaching role: canonical exophytic ovarian-origin graphic. - RadPrimer image 2: Corpus luteum cyst can be exophytic from the ovary ; look for the bridging ovarian parenchyma . Hemorrhage and retracted clot can also be present within a corpus luteum cyst . Teaching role: canonical corpus luteum/hemorrhage example. - RadPrimer image 3: Typical appearance of a simple functional ovarian cyst is shown. Peripheral follicles within surrounding parenchyma confirm an intraovarian cyst. Teaching role: canonical simple functional cyst. - RadPrimer image 4: Ring of fire results from marked peripheral vascular flow around the corpus luteum cyst wall. The cyst has crenulated walls and internal hemorrhagic echoes . Teaching role: canonical ring-of-fire/corpus luteum example. - STATdx image 5: Characteristic lace-like or reticular internal echoes in a hemorrhagic cyst with no internal vascularity. Teaching role: hemorrhagic cyst recognition reinforcement. - STATdx image 6: Color Doppler shows prominent flow in the ovary around the corpus luteum; ring of fire is not specific for ectopic pregnancy. Hemorrhage is present within the corpus luteum cyst . Teaching role: ring-of-fire pitfall. - STATdx image 7: Grayscale ultrasound shows a thick-walled, crenulated corpus luteum related to collapse of the cyst wall after ovulation. Teaching role: corpus luteum morphology reinforcement. - STATdx image 8: Flow is present at the lesion periphery, an expected corpus luteum finding. Teaching role: peripheral-flow reinforcement. - STATdx image 9: Corpus luteum with crenulated margin and internal hemorrhage ; the vascular margin should not be mistaken for malignant solid tissue. Teaching role: vascular-margin pitfall. - STATdx image 10: Longitudinal transvaginal ultrasound shows a 2.55 cm dominant cystic structure in ovarian suppression before superovulation for assisted reproduction; this is a follicular cyst. Teaching role: follicular cyst in fertility-treatment context. - STATdx image 11: Hemorrhagic cyst with internal reticular echogenicity and moderate pelvic free fluid from rupture. Teaching role: ruptured hemorrhagic cyst complication. - STATdx image 12: Large functional cyst with surrounding ovarian parenchyma compressed to a thin rim ; pulse Doppler should confirm arterial and venous waveforms when pelvic pain is present. Teaching role: large cyst/torsion-evaluation context. - STATdx image 13: Corpus luteum cyst with posterior fluid-debris level , consistent with resolving hemorrhagic cyst. Teaching role: resolving hemorrhagic cyst variant. - STATdx image 14: Color Doppler shows a solid-appearing corpus luteum cyst with increased vascularity, similar to ring of fire. Teaching role: solid-appearing corpus luteum pitfall. ARCHIVED DUPLICATE IMAGE NOTES - STATdx image 1 is an exact duplicate of RadPrimer image 1 by stable source image ID and visual evidence; archive by default. - STATdx image 2 is an exact duplicate of RadPrimer image 2 by stable source image ID and visual evidence; archive by default. - STATdx image 3 is an exact duplicate of RadPrimer image 3 by stable source image ID and visual evidence; archive by default. - STATdx image 4 is an exact duplicate of RadPrimer image 4 by stable source image ID and visual evidence; archive by default. GENERATOR NOTES - Use RadPrimer hierarchy/deck routing exactly as supplied in metadata.json. - Use source labels in later prose when a detail is source-specific. - Use clean image labels such as RadPrimer image 4 or STATdx image 11 in narrative-facing text; keep short IDs only in traceability metadata. - Do not generate cards or a lecture from this package yet.

keptText: definitions of follicle, follicular cyst, corpus luteum, and corpus luteum cyst
US appearance of simple/follicular and corpus luteum/hemorrhagic cysts
differential diagnosis against ectopic pregnancy, heterotopic pregnancy, and ovarian neoplasm
pathology, pregnancy behavior, clinical presentation, and management

STATdx.role: Supplemental depth and expanded image-recognition set.
keptText: O-RADS 2022 wording for selected follow-up thresholds
pitfall emphasis that ring of fire is not specific for ectopic pregnancy
additional examples of hemorrhagic cyst, crenulated corpus luteum, rupture/free fluid, large cysts, and resolving debris-level cysts
limitations: STATdx breadcrumb is not used for canonical hierarchy because RadPrimer is present. STATdx images 1-4 duplicate RadPrimer images 1-4 and are archived by default.
